newsitem.title: USA: Japanese man out-eats American hot dog.
newsitem.headline: Japanese man out-eats American hot dog.

text.p: Hirofumi Nakajima can scoff down a couple of hot dogs in less than a New York minute.

The slightly-built 22-year-old from Japan munched his way through more than 23 hot dogs and buns in 12 minutes on Wednesday to win a contest against a strapping American that was billed as the World Cup of competitive eating.

In a boorish atmosphere akin to a professional wrestling show -- complete with a pre-match staring contest and a bejeweled mustard yellow belt as the prize -- Nakajima ate almost three more of the greasy hot dogs than Ed "The Animal" Krachie in the allotted 12 minutes.

"When I walked into the room and heard all those people cheering for the American, I just had to win it," the 144-pound (65-kg) Nakajima told reporters in the Manhattan hot dog restaurant where the event was staged.

Krachie had set the world record in July 1996 by eating 22 hot dogs and buns in the same time period. On Wednesday, Nakajima, the Japanese national eating champion, ate 23-1/4 hot dogs to the American's 21.

About 70 spectators, some of them with their faces pressed against the front window of the Nathan's Famous restaurant, saw Nakajima methodically defeat the 320 pound (145 kg) Krachie, who stands 6 feet 6 inches (1.9 metres) tall.

While the American stood over the table wolfing each hot dog and bun in huge bites, shaking his head and washing them down with water, Nakajima sat with quiet concentration, first eating the meat and then dunking the bread in water before swallowing it.
New Yorker Krachie remained proud, though, despite defeat. "I'm still cocky. I'm still good," he growled.
